title: Geometric compactification and quasi-finite boundary of the good-curves preimage
statement: Let $X,V$ be Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $f:X\to V$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For a finite family indexed by $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $t_i:T_i\to V$ be finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], $j_i:Y_i\to\overline Y_i$ open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and $p_i:\overline Y_i\to T_i$ smooth and proper [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume each $p_i j_i$ is smooth and surjective and each fibre of $p_i$ is geometrically connected of dimension at most one [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\nu:\coprod_iY_i\to X$ be finite and surjective, with $f\nu\iota_i=t_i p_i j_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Let $W\subset X$ be open whose inverse image in each $Y_i$ is dense in every fibre of $p_i j_i$. Put $C=\coprod_i\overline Y_i$ and $P=(\coprod_iY_i)\times_X W$. Then $C$ is Noetherian, its natural map $c:C\to V$ is proper, and there exist an open $O\subset C$ and an isomorphism $e:P\simeq O$ over $V$ and a closed immersion $i:Z\to C$ with image $C\setminus O$, such that $ci$ is quasi-finite [def-weil-closed-immersion] [pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: Define a: coproduct Y_i to coproduct Ybar_i by j_i on each summand. Its component images are disjoint and open, so Mathlib isOpenImmersion_sigmaDesc proves a is an open immersion. The coproduct universal property and hcomm give a followed by c = nu followed by f. Compose a with the first projection of P=(coproduct Y_i) times_X W; this is an open immersion q. Define O as opensRange q and e as q.isoOpensRange. This gives the required isomorphism and compatibility over V. Each p_i followed by t_i is proper. A private proved helper applies induction_empty_option to the finite indexing type: the empty coproduct is empty and proper; sigmaOptionIso reduces the option step to proper_coproduct_two; equivalences of index types transport properness. Thus c is proper. Locally finite type over the Noetherian V gives local Noetherianity of C, and quasi-compactness of c gives compactness, hence C is Noetherian. No separate finite-coproduct compactness or local finite presentation assertion is needed.

proof.text: Let U_i be the inverse image of W under Y_i to X, D_i its open subscheme, and v_i:D_i to Ybar_i its inclusion followed by j_i. Surjectivity of j_i followed by p_i supplies a point in its fibre at s. The density hypothesis hWi then supplies a fibre point lying in U_i. The fibre homeomorphism produces a point of the fibre of v_i followed by p_i. Surjectivity also proves that every fibre of p_i is nonempty. The union of the images of v_i followed by the coprojections equals O: use range_pullback_fst and the pointwise coproduct cover for both inclusions. To match the universe of the index in good_curves_boundary_quasiFinite, reindex the components by ULift (Fin n). The canonical coproduct isomorphism E identifies the union Oprime of the lifted component opens with O and commutes with the structure maps to V. Apply good_curves_boundary_quasiFinite to this lifted family, with the proved nonempty open fibres and the geometric connectedness and dimension hypotheses from hp. Take Z to be the explicitly constructed vanishing-ideal subscheme of the complement of Oprime. Compose its closed immersion into the lifted coproduct with E.hom. The homeomorphism E sends this complement onto the complement of O. The equality E.hom followed by c = the lifted structure map identifies the composite Z to V with goodCurvesBoundaryMap, whose quasi-finiteness is the second conclusion of the stated boundary lemma. All constructions allow n=0 and empty fibres or schemes wherever the hypotheses do.

theorem goodCurvesPreimage_boundary
    {X V : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian V]
    (f : X ⟶ V) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (n : ℕ) (T Y Ybar : Fin n → Scheme.{u})
    (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Ybar i) (p : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ T i)
    (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ X) [IsFinite ν] [Surjective ν]
    (hcomm : ∀ i, Limits.Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ f = j i ≫ p i ≫ t i)
    (ht : ∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.Etale (t i))
    (hj : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i))
    (hjp : ∀ i, Smooth (j i ≫ p i) ∧ Surjective (j i ≫ p i))
    (hp : ∀ i, Smooth (p i) ∧ IsProper (p i) ∧
      ∀ s : T i, GeometricallyConnected ((p i).fiberToSpecResidueField s) ∧
        topologicalKrullDim ((p i).fiber s) ≤ 1)
    (W : X.Opens)
    (hWi : ∀ (i : Fin n) (s : T i),
      Dense (((j i ≫ p i).fiberι s ≫ Limits.Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) ⁻¹' (W : Set X)))
    : IsNoetherian (∐ Ybar) ∧
      IsProper (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i ↦ p i ≫ t i) ∧
      ∃ (O : (∐ Ybar : Scheme.{u}).Opens)
        (e : Limits.pullback ν W.ι ≅ O.toScheme)
        (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ (∐ Ybar)),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧ Set.range i.base = (O : Set (∐ Ybar : Scheme.{u}))ᶜ ∧
        e.hom ≫ O.ι ≫ (Limits.Sigma.desc fun k ↦ p k ≫ t k) =
          Limits.pullback.snd ν W.ι ≫ W.ι ≫ f ∧
        (i ≫ (Limits.Sigma.desc fun k ↦ p k ≫ t k)).IsQuasiFinite
